name: outreach_inmail
description: Prompt for LinkedIn InMail (subject + body) to a non-connection
content:
INPUT:
Contact Information: {contact_info}
Outreach Trigger Information: {trigger_info}
Company Offerings: {offerings}
{project_brief}Company Case Studies: {case_studies}
Company Social Proofs: {social_proofs}
Additional info:
{custom_params}
{tone_analysis_section}
{pain_point_section}
{signal_strategy}

This is a LinkedIn InMail to someone who is NOT a 1st-degree connection. They may already have a pending invitation from us; writing them here is an intentional escalation, not a duplicate pitch.
Primary goal is a short reply, not a meeting booking.
Human, concise, plain English, no hype.
Friendly, not flattering; confident, not pushy.
Avoid emojis, marketing buzzwords, and filler.
Never use LinkedIn-SDR filler: "hands-on", "in the weeds", "hits differently". Do not label the prospect ("as a builder", "as an operator").

{campaign_rules_section}
VOICE: {voice_tone}. Never use: {voice_nogo}.
PRECEDENCE: {message_brief} and campaign rules define WHAT (one paraphrased point). {voice_rules} and anonymity rules below define HOW. Do not name companies, products, titles, or industries unless the brief or campaign rules require that fact.
{message_brief}
PROJECT BRIEF is background. Land only THE BRIEF's one point.
OUTPUT FORMAT (mandatory):
SUBJECT: <one line, under 200 characters>
BODY:
<the InMail body, under 1900 characters>

SUBJECT RULES:
Generate a specific subject from the brief and the prospect's situation. Never reuse a canned subject. No emojis, no exclamation marks, no em dashes, no bracketed placeholder tokens.

BODY STRUCTURE:
2-5 short sentences.
Open with a vague, understated observation about the prospect's situation (paraphrased from their activity, never quoting exact words or naming specifics).
End with ONE question about THEIR daily experience -- not about trends, AI, or industry shifts.
Do NOT mention your product, tool, or how you solve anything unless the campaign rules or brief explicitly require it.
Keep to one question max.

{voice_rules}
ANTI-PATTERNS (InMail — keep these):
- Do not mention any company names, product names, or place names from the prospect's content unless the brief or campaign rules require that fact.
- Do not pitch unless the campaign rules or brief explicitly require it.
- Do not mention the pending invitation, InMail credits, or that this is an InMail.

Guardrails (hard rules):
Do not mention pricing unless the brief requires it.
Do not use or reference any company names at all (theirs or ours) unless the brief requires it, including abbreviations, initials, or bracketed placeholder tokens of any kind.
Do not include any links (website, calendar, deck).
Do not use exclamation marks.
Never emit bracketed placeholder tokens of any kind: every fact must be written out or omitted.

BAD: "That 21x gap suggests call cadence and market context may matter more than rapport. How much hands-on work does it take to make those habits repeatable?"
WHY BAD: Points at a specific stat from their content, then wraps it in sales-methodology jargon the sender would not say.

CRITICAL:
* Response **ONLY** with the SUBJECT:/BODY: format above. **NO reasoning.**
* Subject max 200 characters. Body max 1900 characters.
* {symbols_limit}

FINAL REMINDER: never start the body with the prospect's name; never emit [placeholders].
